Subject: Recap + assets from today's extended-context demo

Hi Evan —

Thanks again for taking the demo with us today. Short recap and proposed next steps below so we don’t lose momentum: 

What we covered
- Walked through ingest -> retrieval -> summarization demo using a 50k-word patient-progress packet.
- Showed two runtime strategies: single long-context model (64k variant) vs. chunked hierarchical summarization.
- Looked at token-cost and latency tradeoffs for both.

Key takeaways we captured
- Primary concern: fidelity of summarization for chart-level findings (clinician notes + structured lab values) — you flagged hallucination risk when the source is truncated.
- Desirable SLOs: 95th percentile answer latency < 700ms for short queries, extractive summaries of full encounter within 6s for batch jobs.

Recommended immediate next steps
1) Benchmarks: we attached the demo recording and a CSV with our benchmark runs on comparable anonymized clinical packets. Please review the latency/cost rows highlighted in column D–F.
2) Prompt set: attached the prompt-set we used (scribehealth-v1) — this is the one we recommend as a baseline for your clinical summarization prompts.
3) Pilot proposal: If you’re comfortable, we suggest a 4-week pilot using our rw/long-64k-v1 (quantized) on a small slice of historical encounters plus a fallback chunking policy for edge cases.

Open questions for you
- Do you have specific regulatory constraints around data residency we should account for during the pilot?
- Which 3 clinician queries would you prioritize for verification in the pilot (e.g., MEDS reconciliation, discharge summary, problem-list extraction)?

I’m copying Marissa (solutions) and Neha (inference team) so they can surface model recommendations and an ops checklist.

Thanks — available for a quick 20m tomorrow if helpful.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Evan — great questions. Answers below (summarized) plus links and a suggested pilot configuration.

1) Data residency / hosting- We can run the pilot in US-only regions. If you need on-prem, our Private package supports customer-hosted runtime (we'd ship an appliance or VPC-trained manifest). For the hosted rw/long-64k-v1 we demoed, kernels were executed in our us-west-2 cluster (explicitly US).

2) Error attribution (truncation vs hallucination)- In the benchmark CSV (attached), column G flags the primary failure mode for each test case. High-level: ~62% of fidelity errors we observed were due to truncation of critical sections (e.g., last clinician addendum cut off) and ~28% were model hallucinations on poorly-specified extraction prompts. The remainder were data-quality issues (OCR artifacts, timestamps).

3) Cost comparison (ballpark) for 1k encounters (avg 20k tokens/encounter)
- Single long-model (rw/long-64k-v1, quantized): ~20M tokens processed/month. Estimated hosted inference cost (tokens-in + tokens-out, amortized) = ~$18k–$28k/mo (range driven by sampling temperature and average response length).
- Chunked + hierarchical summarization (rw/7b-chat + compositional aggregator): ~14M tokens processed + orchestration overhead. Estimated cost = ~$9k–$14k/mo.
Notes: these are order-of-magnitude estimates; we can produce a more precise pro-forma if you share representative token-length distributions. Also recommended to include prefix-level caching for repeated queries (saves ~15–30% on typical workloads).

4) Suggested pilot configuration (4 weeks)
- Ingest: 1k de-identified historical encounters into a US-hosted dedicated pilot (Dedicated or Private).
- Arms: A) rw/long-64k-v1 full-context; B) chunked flow using rw/7b-chat + summarizer aggregator.
- Evaluation: canonical prompt set (attached) + a rubric for hallucination (precision on extracted findings) and latency SLOs. We’ll run both arms and provide per-case failure-mode tagging.

5) Prompt-level mitigations for truncation-induced hallucinations
- Add explicit guardrails in the prompt ("If source text is incomplete, say 'source truncated' and ask for context.")
- Use extractive-first templates: request exact spans and verbatim source snippets for high-risk fields (med lists, dosages).
- Implement a soft-fallback policy: if the aggregator detects a low-confidence extraction, escalate to the long-model for that case only.

Links / assets
- Benchmarks & raw CSV: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcDf-extended-context-benchmarks
- Prompt set (baseline): https://docs.redwood.ai/prompts/scribehealth-long-context-v1
- Demo recording: attached to the original email thread.

Next step proposal
- If you’re aligned, we’ll draft a simple Statement of Work (SOW) and pilot order. Can we get verbal approval from procurement by EOD Wednesday to start infra provisioning next week?

Copying Marissa for SOW + Neha for an ops checklist.

Thanks — I’ll also prepare a short pro-forma cost sheet if you want the line-item breakdown.

Best,
Priya
